resources.string: Any practice today starts a streak.
Counted for %1$s: you started around %2$s, before midnight. Your streak is safe.
Tap Start next time and the app knows exactly.
Track your meditation practice together with your friends.
End-to-end encrypted and fully open source.
All four parts, 111,111 each. Repeat rounds come later.
The short refuge meditation you do before starting ngöndro.
Pick as many as you do.
From paper or a spreadsheet; rough is fine.
Your streak so far counts on your own Today screen. Friends only ever see days tracked in the app.
An evening nudge when a streak is at risk. It is scheduled on this phone; nothing leaves it.
Keep it on this phone, or online?
An account adds friends, public streaks and sync between phones. Counts are end-to-end encrypted either way: the server never sees them.
Friends see your streaks, never your counts
A new phone picks up where this one left off
You can make one later in Settings
Accounts are by invitation for now. Open the link you were sent, or type its code.
Type or paste the invitation code, or paste the whole invitation link. Case doesn\'t matter.
We don\'t know this invitation. Check the code, or ask whoever sent it.
No invitation? Ask someone who uses Duongöndro, or keep practising on this phone: you can add an account later in Settings.
Only on this phone for now

An account in a Buddhist practice app says something about your beliefs, which the GDPR treats as special. With your consent the server keeps your email or username, your name, your gender if you give it, your friends, and your public streaks. Your counts stay encrypted on your phones.
I agree that Duongöndro stores this to run my account. I can export or delete it all in Settings.
We send a sign-in link there. Nobody else sees it.
We sent a link to %1$s. Open it on this phone, or type the code from the email.
Eight letters and digits, as in the email. Case doesn\'t matter; O and 0, I and 1 count as the same. Works for 15 minutes.
That code doesn\'t match. Check the email and try again.
Optional. Without an email you sign in with a passkey, your fingerprint or screen lock; a username names that passkey in your password manager.
Letters, digits, dots and underscores. Friends don\'t see it.
Friends see this name next to your streaks.

Polish, Russian, Ukrainian, Czech and Slovak change words by gender: ukończyłaś or ukończyłeś. We use it only to pick those forms, in the app and in what friends see about you. Non-binary gets wording without a gendered form where the language has one.
Next time you sign in with your fingerprint or screen lock. Google Password Manager keeps it, so a new Android phone has it too.
Not now, email me a link instead
If you lose this phone, this code is the only way back to your counts. Nobody else has it, not even us.
Next we\'ll ask for two of these groups, to make sure. O and 0, I and 1 count as the same.
Save it in Google Password Manager instead
Your phone offers the passkey you saved. No passkey on this phone? We email you a link and a code.
Something went wrong. Check your connection and try again.
Lock screens say “A friend practised” instead of the practice.
Your photo stays on this phone: it is not synced or backed up.
Counts logged so far are kept.
Archiving hides the practice from Today and keeps its counts and history.

The code you wrote down when you set up your first phone. Spaces and dashes do not matter. Moving from your other phone with a QR code comes later.
That recovery code does not open this account.

Your account and everything the server holds about you are deleted first.

Your counts stay on this phone but stop syncing. To sync them again, sign in and enter your recovery code.
Signed out. Sign in again to keep syncing.
Only on this phone. An account adds friends, public streaks and sync between phones; your counts stay end-to-end encrypted.
Before signing out here, finish your recovery code: without it, your counts could not come back.

Erase it here and continue? Whatever of it was synced stays in that account.
